youtube.description:
50 Christmas trivia questions from easy to legend 🎄 Santa, carols, movies and traditions from around the world – can you get 40 out of 50?
Comment your score 👇

Subscribe and turn on the bell for a new quiz every day! 🔔

#ChristmasQuiz #ChristmasTrivia #TriviaQuiz #Quiz #GeneralKnowledge #FamilyQuiz

Music: original.
youtube.comment: How many did you get out of 50? 🎄 Which legend question got you? 👇

lines.q: Fifty questions, from easy to legend, and they get harder every round. Keep score! First one: what color is Santa's suit, traditionally?
lines.a: Red! With white fur trim and a black belt.

lines.q: Which reindeer has a glowing red nose?
lines.a: Rudolph! He lights the way through the fog.

lines.q: Christmas Day falls on which date in December?
lines.a: The twenty fifth! Christmas Eve is the night before.

lines.q: What do kids traditionally hang by the fireplace for Santa?
lines.a: Stockings! Hopefully filled by morning.

lines.q: Where does Santa traditionally live?
lines.a: The North Pole! Workshop, elves and all. Nice, five down!

lines.q: Which Christmas plant do people kiss under?
lines.a: Mistletoe! An old tradition that goes back centuries.

lines.q: What do kids in America leave out for Santa on Christmas Eve?
lines.a: Milk and cookies! And often a carrot for the reindeer.

lines.q: In the song, Frosty the Snowman comes to life thanks to an old silk what?
lines.a: Hat! A magic top hat.

lines.q: How many reindeer pull Santa's sleigh, with Rudolph included?
lines.a: Nine! Eight from the famous poem, plus Rudolph.

lines.q: The Grinch's heart is how many sizes too small?
lines.a: Two sizes! Until it grows three sizes in one day. Ten easy ones done. How many did you get?

lines.q: Round two, medium. In Home Alone, where is Kevin's family flying to?
lines.a: Paris! And they leave him behind in Chicago.

lines.q: Who sang All I Want for Christmas Is You, back in nineteen ninety four?
lines.a: Mariah Carey! It climbs the charts again every December.

lines.q: In The Twelve Days of Christmas, what is the gift on the very first day?
lines.a: A partridge in a pear tree! It comes back every single day.

lines.q: Feliz Navidad means Merry Christmas in which language?
lines.a: Spanish! Navidad comes from the Latin word for birth.

lines.q: Ebenezer Scrooge's famous grumpy phrase is Bah, what?
lines.a: Humbug! Great job, fifteen down.

lines.q: According to the Gospels, in which town was Jesus born?
lines.a: Bethlehem! He grew up in Nazareth.

lines.q: Which striped Christmas candy is shaped like a hook?
lines.a: The candy cane! Red and white, usually peppermint.

lines.q: Which creamy Christmas drink is made with milk, sugar and eggs?
lines.a: Eggnog! Often with a splash of rum or brandy.

lines.q: Who plays Buddy in the two thousand three movie Elf?
lines.a: Will Ferrell! Raised by elves at the North Pole.

lines.q: In It's a Wonderful Life, every time a bell rings, an angel gets his what?
lines.a: Wings! Clarence finally earns his. Medium round done. How's your score?

lines.q: Round three, hard. The Christmas tree tradition started mainly in which country?
lines.a: Germany! Prince Albert later made it popular in Britain.

lines.q: What three gifts did the Wise Men bring?
lines.a: Gold, frankincense and myrrh! Two of them are fragrant tree resins.

lines.q: In Japan, which fast food chain is a hugely popular Christmas dinner?
lines.a: K F C! Families even order their bucket weeks ahead.

lines.q: Which Christmas ballet features the Sugar Plum Fairy?
lines.a: The Nutcracker! Music by Tchaikovsky.

lines.q: Who sang White Christmas, the best selling single of all time?
lines.a: Bing Crosby! Written by Irving Berlin. If you're enjoying this, subscribe and turn on the bell!

lines.q: Boxing Day is celebrated on which date?
lines.a: December twenty sixth! The day after Christmas.

lines.q: The famous Christmas truce of nineteen fourteen happened during which war?
lines.a: World War One! Soldiers swapped gifts in no man's land.

lines.q: Which cartoonist drew famous pictures of Santa for Harper's Weekly in the eighteen hundreds?
lines.a: Thomas Nast! He helped shape how Santa looks today.

lines.q: Krampus, the horned Christmas creature, comes from the folklore of which mountains?
lines.a: The Alps! He punishes naughty kids.

lines.q: Who composed Messiah, with its famous Hallelujah chorus?
lines.a: Handel! Hard round finished. Still with me?

lines.q: Round four, very hard. Which red Christmas plant is named after an American diplomat?
lines.a: The poinsettia! After Joel Poinsett, the first US minister to Mexico.

lines.q: Rudolph the red nosed reindeer was created in nineteen thirty nine for which store?
lines.a: Montgomery Ward! As a free coloring book for shoppers.

lines.q: Silent Night was first performed in which country?
lines.a: Austria! In the village of Oberndorf, in eighteen eighteen.

lines.q: In which year was the first commercial Christmas card sold?
lines.a: Eighteen forty three! The same year A Christmas Carol came out.

lines.q: The real Saint Nicholas was a bishop in which modern day country?
lines.a: Turkey! In the town of Myra. Thirty five down, nice work!

lines.q: Which friendly Italian witch brings gifts on Epiphany?
lines.a: La Befana! She flies on a broomstick on January sixth.

lines.q: Which tall, sweet Christmas bread comes from Milan?
lines.a: Panettone! Full of raisins and candied fruit.

lines.q: Mele Kalikimaka means Merry Christmas in which language?
lines.a: Hawaiian! It's the Hawaiian way to say Merry Christmas.

lines.q: In Iceland, how many Yule Lads visit children before Christmas?
lines.a: Thirteen! One each night, all of them pranksters.

lines.q: Which president made Christmas a federal holiday in eighteen seventy?
lines.a: Ulysses S Grant! Very hard round done!

lines.q: Final round, legend! How many gifts are given in total in The Twelve Days of Christmas?
lines.a: Three hundred sixty four! Almost one for every day of the year.

lines.q: Which artist painted Coca-Cola's famous Santa ads, starting in nineteen thirty one?
lines.a: Haddon Sundblom! Coca-Cola didn't invent Santa, though.

lines.q: In the original eighteen twenty three poem, the last two reindeer were Dunder and who?
lines.a: Blixem! Dutch for thunder and lightning. They became Donner and Blitzen.

lines.q: In ten eighty seven, Saint Nicholas's remains were taken to which Italian city?
lines.a: Bari! Sailors carried them from Myra.

lines.q: Which German city's Striezelmarkt dates back to fourteen thirty four?
lines.a: Dresden! One of the oldest Christmas markets anywhere. Forty five down!

lines.q: Which crew read from the book of Genesis while orbiting the Moon on Christmas Eve?
lines.a: Apollo eight! In nineteen sixty eight.

lines.q: In the sixteen forties, who banned Christmas in England?
lines.a: The Puritans! Christmas came back in sixteen sixty.

lines.q: Three left, stay with me! Which Christmas song was played in space in nineteen sixty five?
lines.a: Jingle Bells! Gemini six astronauts played harmonica and bells.

lines.q: On December thirteenth, which country celebrates Saint Lucia with crowns of candles?
lines.a: Sweden! Girls in white gowns sing in the dark.

lines.q: Final question. The first electric Christmas tree lights, in eighteen eighty two, came from a partner of which inventor?
lines.a: Thomas Edison! His partner Edward Johnson strung up eighty bulbs. Merry Christmas, you made it to the end!
